chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about a man who forgot that he had not bowed (ruku') until he prostrated (sajdah) and stood up. He said: 'He should begin again.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to bow in prayer and goes straight to prostration?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific fiqh of *nasi* (forgetfulness) where a worshipper omits the ruku' entirely before moving to sajdah. While the Arabic text 'yastaqbil' literally means 'he faces [the direction]' or 'he stands', in the context of the chapter on mistakes during ruku', it is interpreted by Shia jurists as the individual remaining in the current state or restarting the rak'ah from the point of error, highlighting the precision required in maintaining the order of prayer pillars (arkan). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the structural integrity of the prayer, distinguishing between minor omissions that require a single prostration of forgetfulness (sajdat al-nasi) and major structural errors that necessitate restarting the unit.
